body:
Part of the worlds design program: [#5955](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5955). Statements S75–S76 of the 2026-11-04 brief.

## Requirement (Drew, in substance)

- Worlds could **build their own rules**, **pre-approve specific designs**, and build **content moderation, approval, or report capabilities**.
- The best ones could end up as **libraries, which could be reused by different worlds** — and then it would be standard because it's **literally the same thing** from a different world, but maybe with a **different set of moderators or reviewers or approvers**, or a **different threshold for reports to have automatic quarantine**.

So moderation is not a platform feature bolted on top: it is **world code**, subject to the same library model as everything else in this program — typed, attachable, importable, parameterized per world.

## Design points to settle

- The moderation-library interface: what hooks exist (submission approval, report intake, quarantine action, appeal), and which are world-provided vs platform-provided. A moderation library receives capabilities like any other code — which means its powers are exactly the platform surface passed to it (programming-model child of [#5955](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5955)); say which capability set a moderation library legitimately needs (read content? hide content? ban principals?) and how that interacts with writer-set authority ([#5545](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5545)).
- Parameterization: moderator/reviewer sets and report thresholds are **per-world configuration** of the same library — config, not forks. KDL profile ([#5753](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5753)).
- Pre-approval of designs: what is a "design" here (a world object submission? a library? a user function?) and what does approval bind (content hash, capability set)?
- Relation to the boards moderation line: [#5680](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5680) and its hooks split [#5861](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5861) are board-surface designs; this issue is the world-level generalization. Cross-pollinate, don't duplicate.

## Related

- Boards next steps / moderation hooks: [#5680](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5680), [#5861](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5861)
- Sharing & permissions cluster (knowledge layer): [#5840](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5840)
- Library typing child of [#5955](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5955) (a moderation system is a library with an attachment and a capability footprint)

## Done looks like

A design doc: moderation-as-library interface, per-world parameterization model, pre-approval semantics, and the capability/authority set a moderation library runs with.
